summary: Round 2 implementation review of the frozen uncommitted snapshot (manifest 93d5fdcb...). The sole round-1 blocking defect IMPL-R1-001 is fixed: contracts.admission_from_budget (contracts.py:26-27) calls budget.committed() and budget.allocation_snapshot(), StageTask.prepare (stages.py:81) uses it, and I confirmed in the pinned gpu_budget.py that committed is a @_locked method (line 263), allocation_snapshot returns a tuple of dicts carrying 'capacity' (186-188), and the only off-ledger reserve/release path is gpu_shared_constants (lines 88/93/118), which is not engaged because the runner requires _n_bd_per_gpu == 1 and can_share needs more than one device peer. host_native_check.py exercises the real _GpuBudget plus StageTask.prepare and the S-stage callback under a host CUDA mock; checks-02.json reports 65/65 unit tests and 8/8 host checks (not re-executed by me). IMPL-R1-002 is materially improved but not closed: the new SeedReader._sampled path derives seed offsets from native Dgram views, compares every XTC header and Shapes byte per record, checks timestamp/service/size and file identity, and rejects same-size layout changes, truncation and short reads (16 reference tests); the pixel-to-word mapping (selected // 10 against np.repeat(seed, 10)[:PIXELS]) and the CPU-v3 constant packing ((4, npix, 2) indexed by gain bits, size_blk unused) match the native UtilsDetector.cc kernel; native-reference-parity.json shows bitwise equality on three real events. However the reference walltime ceiling remains unmeasured (see IMPL-R2-001, non-blocking). IMPL-R1-003 (setup-time CuPy weakref probe, stages.py:73-79, recorded per BD), IMPL-R1-004 (two memory queries per callback in every stage, labelled in processing_instrumentation) and IMPL-R1-005 (all four optional shared attributes and both flags recorded per rank, runner.py:120-122, 231-232) are resolved. No regressions found: keepalive lifetime with n_gpu_streams=1 means EventPool depth 1, so submit refuses an occupied slot and release_storage clears producer_owners before the next callback, making the 'previous full-image owner retained' weakref gate consistent with the pinned runtime; cube.drain precedes that check so the cube's pending owners do not false-trigger it; the calibration kernel cache key built in prepare matches the key calibrate() computes (device 0, 32 segments, ctypes in calibconst order, with_validity False) so no JIT occurs in the timed loop. PLAN-R2-001: CopyAudit is valid; it wraps the live PublicationD2H instance that _submit_gpu calls (gpu_events.py:834), every _destination decision passes through the wrapper, zero-byte groups are excluded from fallback counting consistent with _destination's nbytes==0 early return, pinned_capacity_high is exact because capacity changes only inside _destination, and the result labels itself as harness wrappers rather than CUDA profiling; acceptance-only .get() transfers and the bounded export D2H are deliberately outside it. PLAN-R2-002: the hash-identical receipt copy pins identical native source hashes in both trees and every loaded .so; only psana/meson.build differs; the newly used native interfaces (Dgram view/config_names decoding, utilsdetector_ext calib_jungfrau_v3, calib_xtc roundtrip, dgramedit for fixtures) ran on the pinned binaries in the host checks; the GPU path is Python/CuPy with no rebuild. This compute compatibility strategy is acceptable for preparing the job only; it proves no new build compatibility, no GPU test has executed, and the allocation-time 31-pass regressions, 10 descriptor guards, two full-pixel bitwise ECC acceptance cases and admission ledger checks remain mandatory. PLAN-R2-003: PS_JF_SHARE_DERIVED and PS_GEO_SHARE are pinned to '0' in launch env and re-checked in the runner; mpi_ds.py returns at lines 266-268 and 330-332 before creating _jungfrau_shared_mem, _geo_shared_mem, _shared_geo_cache or _shared_calibc_cache, and the runner asserts and records their absence. Node availability is recorded as unconfirmed with no reservation claim (availability-latest.json, manifest node_availability). No job is submitted or authorized by this review.

findings.evidence: Residual of IMPL-R1-002. The full-run reference ceiling is 600 s and the whole-case ceiling that launch.py actually enforces (launch.py:331, 339, 351 via case_seconds) is 1980 s for every full cell. native-reference-parity.json records warm sampled reads of about 6 ms/event (485 preads of <=68 bytes per event) on sdfiana025 against the original scratch copy; at 100,000 events that is about 600 s before any CPU-v3 and FP64 work, already equal to the reference component. In the job, rank 0 reads the Weka stage after processing, when page cache was evicted before processing and at most about 192 GB of the 336 GB input can be resident, so a large share of the roughly 48 million small preads will be cold network fetches whose latency is unmeasured. CubeReference iterates bin by bin (reference.py:304), stride 99 events in file order, which defeats readahead. If the first full ECC cell (case 11) exceeds 1980 s, run_owned raises, main() writes incomplete_not_accepted and the campaign ends with three full cells completed. basis.kind is declared conservative_unmeasured and the behaviour is fail-closed, so this is not a correctness or safety defect, but it is the most likely way this preparation fails to deliver the requested comparison.
findings.requested_change: Before submission, either (a) add a measured basis: a short host-only timing of SeedReader.raw(timestamp, samples()) over a few hundred events against a cold (fadvise DONTNEED) Weka copy, and set the full reference ceiling and case ceiling from that measurement with margin, or (b) restructure CubeReference to gather all sampled seed words for all 100,000 events in one file-order pass into a bounded host buffer (100000 x 32 x 16 x 2 bytes, about 100 MB) before per-bin validation so the OS can read ahead, keeping every existing identity/layout check, or (c) raise the full reference and case ceilings with explicit justification and re-run validate_budget. Keep fail-closed behaviour; do not shorten event counts or skip bins.

findings.evidence: SeedReader.__init__ indexes every record by reading a 24-byte header at each datagram position for all five streams until all requested timestamps are found (about 500,000 cold preads at 3.3 MB stride for a 100,000-event ECC case). The runner constructs this reader on rank 0 for every ECC case (runner.py:145) before cache conditioning, so the I/O is correctly excluded from the timed interval and from the NIC evidence window, but it counts against the same 1980 s whole-case ceiling as processing, export and reference, while budget.json reserves only 120 s for setup. The three-event parity run indexed only the file prefix and does not bound this cost.
findings.requested_change: Document the index-scan cost as part of the reference/setup budget justification, or fold a one-time measured index-scan duration into the case ceiling together with IMPL-R2-001; alternatively cache the per-stream offset table on rank 0 across cases of one campaign (host-only, identity-checked against st_ino/size/mtime) so only the first ECC case pays the scan. No change to processing timing or gates is required.
